title: MITRE ATLAS: The Complete Guide for Security Teams
content_md: Key Takeaways MITRE ATLAS, short for Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems, is a MITRE-maintained framework developed with industry partners and AI security researchers to map adversary tactics and techniques against AI and machine learning systems. ATLAS has 16 tactics laid out like ATT&CK, with 14 sharing the same names. Each tactic groups techniques describing specific attack methods, and those techniques link to case studies documenting real incidents against AI systems. ATLAS uses case studies instead of ATT&CK's Procedures layer because no catalog of named threat actor groups exists for AI attacks. Most documented AI incidents come from academic research or red team exercises rather than tracked adversary activity. Two ATLAS tactics have no ATT&CK equivalent. AI Attack Adaptation covers how attackers tailor and test capabilities against a specific AI target before and during an operation. AI Model Access defines four attacker access modes, from an inference API to full model weights to physical proximity to the hardware, which determine which techniques are available.
